issues.description: Default speaker mismatch between docs and config for bulbul:v3-beta
issues.detail: The PR description and docstrings state v3 default speaker is 'aditya', but TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS sets default_speaker='shubh'. Pick one source of truth. The data table is the contract; the config is the implementation. Fix the data so the algorithm is self-evident.

issues.description: Two parallel registries describe the same data (Enums + tuple in config)
issues.detail: SarvamTTSSpeakerV2/V3 enums and TTS_MODEL_CONFIGS.speakers encode the same speaker list twice. Pick one. The speaker list is data; keep it in the config dict and let callers iterate. The enum buys type-safety at the cost of duplication you must keep in sync.

issues.description: ModelConfig dataclasses are fine, but a plain dict would do the same work
issues.detail: Two frozen dataclasses (ModelConfig, TTSModelConfig) each used by exactly one lookup table. A dict-of-dicts would carry the same information in less code. Acceptable as-is since frozen=True documents intent, but resist the urge to grow more fields here; that path leads to a framework.

issues.description: Silent clamping of pace masks caller errors
issues.detail: If the caller passes pace=5.0 for v3, the code logs a warning and clamps to 2.0. Pydantic already validates ge/le on the field for the wider v2 range. Either reject at construction with a clear error (consistent with prompt/mode/language validation) or document the policy explicitly. Mixed strategies confuse callers.

issues.description: get_speakers_for_model silently falls back to v2 for unknown models
issues.detail: Returning v2 speakers for an unknown model name is a quiet wrong answer. The constructor already rejects unknown models with ValueError; this helper should do the same, or return an empty list. Silent defaults make bugs travel.

Code logs 'pitch parameter is ignored' only when params.pitch != 0.0. But the default 0.0 is a real value the caller may have passed intentionally. Just log once at construction if the model doesn't support pitch and the caller didn't explicitly opt in via Optional sentinel (None). Defaulting to 0.0 then comparing to 0.0 is fighting the data shape.

review.summary: The refactor moves from string-sniffing model names ('saaras' in model.lower()) to a table-driven config. That is the right direction: the data now dominates, the branches collapse. Two things to clean up: the speaker list is duplicated between Enums and the config tuple, and the v3 default speaker disagrees between docs (aditya) and config (shubh) — pick one source of truth. Minor: silent clamping and silent fallbacks should either raise like the rest of the validation or be documented as policy. Overall this is smaller and more obvious than what it replaced.
